items.title: آنچه گذشت: کشته شدن دو ایتالیایی در حمله پهپادی؛ کویت سفیر ایران را احضار کرد
items.summary: وزارت خارجه کویت اعلام کرد در پی حمله پهپادی روز پنجشنبه که به کشته شدن دو شهروند ایتالیایی در این کشور انجامید، سفیر ایران را احضار کرده است. تهران هرگونه دخالت در این حمله را رد کرده و آمادگی خود را برای همکاری با کویت و ایتالیا به‌منظور شناسایی منشا حمله اعلام کرده است. دولت ایتالیا می‌گوید این دو نفر روی پدافند هوایی کار می‌کردند و در «حمله پهپادی ایران» به مرکز رادار تاسیسات نظامی کویت کشته شدند.

items.title: قیمت دلار در بازار آزاد ایران به مرز ۳۰۰ هزار تومان رسید
items.summary: قیمت هر دلار آمریکا در بازار غیررسمی ارز تهران به ۲۹۸ هزار تومان رسیده و قیمت هر پوند بریتانیا از ۳۹۰ هزار تومان فراتر رفته است. افزایش بهای ارزهای خارجی در ایران در شرایطی ادامه دارد که جنگ و تحریم‌های اقتصادی فشار مضاعفی بر اقتصاد آن کشور وارد کرده است. کاهش ارزش پول ملی ایران، علاوه بر افزایش هزینه واردات کالا و مواد اولیه مورد نیاز تولید، می‌تواند به تشدید تورم و کاهش بیشتر قدرت خرید مردم منجر شود. ادامه فشارهای اقتصادی آمریکا بر ایران و بحران تنگه هرمز نیز بر ابهام‌ها درباره چشم‌انداز اقتصاد ایران افزوده است.

items.summary_original: A Russian-born conservative activist in North Carolina says she is being targeted for her political speech after she was charged with a crime stemming from online interactions with a local Democratic Party official. Liuba Wofford-Keller is an outspoken activist for local Republican candidates and has spoken out against Congressman-elect Richard Ojeda, D-N.C., during this year's election cycle. But Wofford-Keller's online interactions with Lisa Wells, the secretary of the Moore County Democratic Party, led to the Republican activist being charged with cyberstalking under North Carolina law. Wofford-Keller says the charges remind her of the communist regime she left behind in Russia. PROSECUTOR DROPS CASE AGAINST WOMAN ACCUSED OF THREATENING TRUMP ON TIKTOK Over the course of the year, Wofford-Keller engaged multiple times online with Wells. Wofford-Keller describes meeting Wells only twice in person, on North Carolina's primary election day in March and on Election Day in November. She says that in between those two dates, the online fight ensued. Wells is also local precinct chair in Moore County. Those interactions are the basis for a state charge against Wofford-Keller for "embarrassing" Wells online. items.summary_original: As January approaches and newly elected lawmakers prepare to take their oaths of office, past statements could prove troublesome as they jockey for committee assignments with powerbrokers seeking to protect the image of their respective parties. The midterm elections sent a new crop of lawmakers affiliated with the Democratic Socialists of America to Congress — in a few cases, unexpectedly. While some sought to moderate their image after the primary season, controversial remarks made on the campaign trail or years before their candidacies could follow them to Capitol Hill as they seek committee assignments and influence within the Democratic caucus. Fox News Digital reviewed some of the most controversial remarks made by the incoming lawmakers — comments that could complicate their efforts to build influence in the new Congress. items.summary_original: Texas Attorney General -elect Nathan Johnson said this week that he won't defend a law requiring public schools across the state to display the Ten Commandments as the U.S. Supreme Court weighs whether to review the case. In an interview with The Dallas Morning News , Johnson, the first Democrat to be elected Texas attorney general in nearly three decades, called the law "unconstitutional," marking a distinct split with outgoing Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton, who championed the bill. "My jurisprudential opinion is that the law is unconstitutional," Johnson said. "The court will have the ultimate say as to what's constitutional and what is not, but I'm the one who says what the state's position is, and it will not be the position the state has previously taken," he continued. TEXAS DEM JAMES TALARICO RIPS 'UN-CHRISTIAN' COURT DECISION ON WHAT'S ALLOWED IN CLASSROOMS Under state law, Senate Bill 10 requires that a "conspicuous" copy of the Ten Commandments be displayed in every classroom in every public school and open-enrollment charter school across Texas. In April, the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that the law did not violate the Constitution, a major victory for proponents of the legislation, including religious freedom advocates, who have long argued the biblical text is a crucial component of America's legal, moral and historical heritage. items.summary_original: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) announced that Rikers Island would be closed "once and for all" by 2032, a promise one crime expert said doesn't add up and could release violent criminals back onto the streets. Mamdani pledged to replace the city's largest jail with four smaller ones across different boroughs, while corrections officers and criminal justice scholars have raised concerns that shrinking the population of more than 6,000 inmates could carry lasting consequences. Rafael Mangual, head of research for policing and public safety at the Manhattan Institute, told Fox News Digital there won't be enough beds to accommodate a city of nearly 9 million people. "If New York City gets this wrong, make no mistake, there will be a massive hit to public safety ," Mangual said. MAMDANI IN HOT SEAT OVER POST MOURNING DEATH OF INMATE CHARGED WITH CALLOUS CRIME: 'ABSOLUTELY SHAMEFUL' The replacement jails in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx will have a capacity of 4,160 beds, with an additional 340 therapeutic beds for inmates with mental illnesses and other medical needs. They will be placed closer to public transit and courthouses. Mamdani said the decision to push the closure of Rikers back by five years was because of "prior administration delays." The city will also invest $146 million in support services. items.summary_original: The Taliban have reportedly banned the use of women's names in official documents in a northern Afghan province, with some women being referred to by degrading animal names, according to a report by Spanish newspaper El País . The latest assault on women's rights under Taliban rule reportedly extends to medical records and prescriptions in Afghanistan's Balkh province, raising fears that the restrictions could spread nationwide. Healthcare workers and other public employees have been instructed to address women as "Bibi," meaning grandmother or old woman, according to reporting by Afghan news outlet Zan Times and The Guardian cited by El País. MOSCOW, TALIBAN FORGE MILITARY ALLIANCE IN POWER GRAB AFTER US AFGHANISTAN EXIT: REPORTS Afghan women's rights activist Lalah Osmany, who is based in Germany, told El País that testimony from women, doctors and civil rights activists indicates some women are also being referred to in degrading terms such as "goat" or "cow." "This is a systematic process of dehumanization," Osmany told the newspaper. An Afghan activist speaking under a pseudonym confirmed the reported order to El País, although she said it had so far been ignored. Zubaida Akbar, who directs the Afghanistan program at women's rights organization Femena, warned that the Taliban could eventually impose the ban nationwide, citing previous instances in which local restrictions were expanded across the country. items.summary_original: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani approved roughly $850,000 in pay raises for dozens of City Hall aides during his first year in office, according to municipal payroll records reviewed by the New York Post . The records show the raises were distributed to at least 46 staffers since Mamdani took office in January, bringing total compensation increases near $1 million. The Post counted 21 new hires who received raises totaling $450,000 before their first anniversary on the job, more than twice the combined number of first-year employees who got raises under Eric Adams and Bill de Blasio. MAMDANI TURNS ON NEW YORK CITY TEACHERS UNION WITH LAWSUIT BLOCKING PAY RAISES FOR EDUCATORS On Jan. 28, five City Hall employees were granted salary increases totaling $95,000 on the same day Mamdani announced New York City faced an estimated $12 billion budget deficit, the records show. The mayor’s office later lowered that projected deficit to approximately $5.4 billion. The mayor’s office on Nov. 12 confirmed the city’s fiscal 2027 budget rose $3.3 billion from the budget adopted in June, reaching $129.2 billion. items.summary: در نوامبر 1966، 12 سرباز آمریکایی مستقر در یک پاسگاه منزوی در یک منطقه جنگی ویتنام، تا آنجا که می توانستند از جشن سنتی شکرگزاری در خانه دور بودند. تنها وسیله تامین مجدد آنها از طریق هوا بود. اما ارتش ایالات متحده مصمم بود که به هر حال شام روز شکرگزاری را برای آنها فراهم کند. طبق سوابق وزارت دفاع که توسط آرشیو ملی حفظ شده است، یک گروهبان در Bien Hoa، بوقلمون و همه چیزهای تزئینی را آماده کرد، غذا را در ظروف عایق بندی شده بسته بندی کرد و با هلیکوپتر به منطقه جنگی D فرستاد، جایی که سه افسر و 9 مرد سرباز از یگان پنجم نیروی ویژه برای شام شکرگزاری نشستند. این تحویل بخشی از تلاش‌های لجستیکی عظیمی بود که ارتش ایالات متحده در طول جنگ‌های نسل‌های متمادی برای رساندن وعده‌های غذایی سنتی روز شکرگزاری به سربازان انجام داده است.
items.summary_original: In November 1966, 12 American soldiers stationed at an isolated outpost in a Vietnamese war zone were about as far from a traditional Thanksgiving at home as they could get. Their only means of resupply was by air. But the U.S. military was determined to get them Thanksgiving dinner anyway. A mess sergeant at Bien Hoa prepared turkey and all the trimmings, packed the meal into insulated containers and sent it by helicopter into War Zone D, where three officers and nine enlisted men of a 5th Special Forces detachment sat down to Thanksgiving dinner, according to Defense Department records preserved by the National Archives. The delivery was one piece of a massive logistical effort the U.S. military has undertaken during wars spanning generations to get traditional Thanksgiving meals to troops serving in combat zones. From civilians sending tens of thousands of turkeys to Union troops during the Civil War to helicopters carrying hot meals to soldiers in Korea, the holiday has been observed through some of the nation's most consequential conflicts. Thanksgiving became a national tradition in the midst of war. President Abraham Lincoln issued his 1863 Thanksgiving proclamation as the Civil War entered its third year, calling on Americans to observe the final Thursday of November as a day of "Thanksgiving and Praise." items.summary_original: Beginning in the new year, minors will be required to pass a five-step seat belt fit test before they can ride without a booster seat or sit in the front seat of a vehicle. The bill's author, Assemblymember Lori Wilson, cited figures showing that child injuries and fatalities in crashes have risen since the pandemic, with children ages 8 to 12 disproportionately affected. "Extending the required age for booster use and implementing straightforward testing can significantly enhance child safety," CalMatters reported. "So the best thing to do to keep your child safe while riding in a vehicle matches what our law is," Wilson said of the bill in April 2025. "It really is to take into consideration all the varying types of seats that we sit on in the car. This is about safety. "This is about making sure that if something happens, you are safe, and I think that’s the key thing that we’re trying to drive home is that it is not about treating people like babies." 3 CAR SEAT INSTALLATION MISTAKES YOU NEED TO AVOID Previously, children ages 8 and older — or those at least 4 feet, 9 inches tall — could ride without a booster seat. In 2020, Obama's "A Promised Land" sold more than 800,000 copies within the first 24 hours of publication, reaching 1 million copies sold by the end of its first week. Clinton's "My Life" hit the 1 million copies benchmark within two weeks of its release. items.summary_original: A rural Oxfordshire village of just over 350 people is taking on the British government, finding itself at the center of a national debate over immigration and public safety. Residents of Piddington, a small community about 10 miles from the famous Oxford University and known more for its rural setting and centuries-old parish church than political activism, voted overwhelmingly in September to secede from the United Kingdom in a symbolic referendum. The 285-26 vote came after residents learned Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s government planned to house more than 1,200 male asylum seekers at a former Ministry of Defence base in Bicester — less than a mile from the village. What began as a local planning dispute has since become one of Britain's most closely watched immigration battles. The controversy intensified earlier this month when the government approved plans for the asylum accommodation center despite objections from local officials, residents and the Thames Valley Police and Crime Commissioner. items.summary_original: Andrea Stewart-Cousins, the trailblazing majority leader of the New York State Senate, has died at age 76, according to multiple reports. Stewart-Cousins, the first Black woman to lead the state's upper chamber, was found dead in her Yonkers home on Friday morning, police sources told the New York Post . Her daughter reportedly tried to get in touch with her on Thursday night before calling for a welfare check. Stewart-Cousins, a Democrat, was first elected to the state senate in 2007. She then became majority leader in January 2019 after Democrats won a majority in the chamber in the 2018 midterm elections. NYC MAYOR MAMDANI ANNOUNCES DELAYED PLAN TO CLOSE CITY'S LARGEST JAIL "She was a groundbreaking leader who shattered one of New York ’s highest glass ceilings," Mike Murphy, a spokesman for the Democratic majority, said in a statement. Stewart-Cousins entered a state government marked by a tumultuous Democratic conference amid feuds and power struggles, Politico reported. In 2018, Democrats eventually won 39 of the state Senate’s 63 seats, giving the party its first stable majority since World War II. The next year, state lawmakers spent their time addressing progressive pieces of legislation, such as immigration, abortion protections and tenants' rights, according to the report. items.summary: یک هواپیمای ارتش آمریکا روز پنجشنبه یک کشتی تجاری را در خلیج عمان پس از اینکه تلاش کرد از محاصره دریایی تمام بنادر ایران که از اواسط ژوئیه اجرایی شده بود دور بزند، از کار انداخت. M/V Pacific Archer با پرچم پالائو، بندرعباس، شهر بندری مهم در سواحل جنوبی ایران را ترک کرد، قبل از اینکه فرماندهی مرکزی ایالات متحده (CENTCOM) مهمات دقیق را به سمت عقب کشتی شلیک کرد و نیروی محرکه آن را نابود کرد. ویدئویی که توسط ارتش منتشر شده است نشان می دهد که یک پرتابه به پشت کشتی برخورد می کند و باعث انفجار می شود. سنتکام گفت که خدمه غیرنظامی در این حمله آسیبی ندیده اند. تاکنون، نیروهای ایالات متحده 158 کشتی تجاری منطبق را تغییر مسیر داده و 6 فروند کشتی را که از رعایت آنها خودداری کرده اند، از کار انداخته اند. دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا گفت: ترامپ به ایران جرأت می‌کند که محاصره بندر آمریکا را زیر پا بگذارد در حالی که تهران طبق گزارش‌ها آماده 14 نفتکش است.
items.summary_original: A U.S. military aircraft disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday after it tried to evade the naval blockade of all Iranian ports, which has been in effect since mid-July. The Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer left Bandar Abbas, a major port city on Iran's southern coast, before the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) fired precision munitions at the ship's stern, destroying its propulsion. A video released by the military shows a projectile hitting the back of the ship and causing an explosion. The civilian crew was unharmed in the strike, CENTCOM said. So far, U.S. forces have redirected 158 compliant commercial vessels and disabled six that refused to comply. TRUMP DARES IRAN TO BREACH US PORT BLOCKADE AS TEHRAN REPORTEDLY READIES 14 OIL TANKERS President Donald Trump said Thursday, while celebrating Thanksgiving at Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida, that victory in the Iran war would come "whenever I want it." "We have victory at hand. It's going to be whenever, sort of, whatever I want it to be. To be honest, and we're trying to be nice, we're giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives. But I am not sure if they are going to take advantage of that," he said in a phone call to U.S. service members. Trump also praised U.S. troops for their role in preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. "در ابتدا تصور می شد که بروس به آرامی در خانه از بین رفته است. پس از تحقیقات بیشتر، معلوم شد که بروس تصمیم گرفته به زندگی خود پایان دهد." در ادامه این بیانیه آمده است: «خانواده از ابراز همدردی اخیر برای فقدان خود عمیقاً قدردانی می کنند و در این ایام سوگواری خواستار درک هستند. شوهر سناتور جمهوری خواه مرد: خانواده ما هستند

items.summary: به گفته یک خلبان F-16، دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا در طی یک تماس تلفنی در روز شکرگزاری متوجه شد که "بزرگترین" جت جنگنده جهان چیست. "پس می‌توانم بپرسم، قبل از اینکه سخنرانی کوچکم را برای شما انجام دهم - کمی سریع - آیا می‌توانم بپرسم، بنابراین F-16، شما آن را دوست دارید، درست است؟" ترامپ از سرهنگ دوم نیروی هوایی آمریکا برانت اسمیت پرسید. اسمیت پاسخ داد: "بزرگترین جت جنگنده جهان، قربان." هنگامی که رئیس جمهور و ملانیا، بانوی اول، با اعضای هر شش شاخه ارتش ایالات متحده تماس گرفتند، ترامپ از استراحتگاه مار-آ-لاگو در فلوریدا با اسمیت صحبت کرد. نگاهی به نحوه گذراندن تعطیلات شکرگزاری ترامپ در طول سال ها ترامپ از اسمیت خواست که F-16 خود را با جت های جنگنده دیگری مانند F-22 یا F-35 مقایسه کند، که اسمیت پاسخ داد: "F-16 تمام روز." ترامپ می گوید خلبانان نیروی هوایی یک پرواز یوفو گرد را توصیف کردند
items.summary_original: President Donald Trump learned what the "world's greatest" fighter jet is, according to an F-16 pilot, during a phone call on Thanksgiving Day. "So could I ask, before I give my little speech to you — a little quick one — could I ask, so the F-16, you love it, right?" Trump asked U.S. Air Force Lt. Col. Brant Smith. "World's greatest fighter jet, sir," Smith replied. items.summary_original: On the heels of the blue wave in the 2026 U.S. midterms, incoming Democratic leaders are tapping an eclectic mix of political veterans, business executives and entertainment figures to help shape their transitions into power. From a Hollywood mogul and former Biden administration officials to figures with ties to Republican leaders, the appointments offer an early glimpse into the people Democrats are turning to as they prepare to govern — and the experience and connections they hope to bring into their new administrations. Several incoming Democrats are turning to familiar faces from the Biden administration. In New Mexico, Gov.-elect Deb Haaland tapped former Biden presidential speechwriter Felicia Salazar and former Interior Department official Joan Mooney for her transition team, while California Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra selected Arsenio Mataka, who previously served as his senior counselor at the Department of Health and Human Services under Biden, to direct policy for his transition team. In Ohio, Democratic Gov.-elect Amy Acton tapped Elisabeth Hire, a former aide to then-Vice President Biden, as a transition co-chair. Haaland's campaign and Becerra's campaign each did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Visa Business and Economics Insights انتظار دارد فروش تعطیلات 4.5 درصد نسبت به سال گذشته افزایش یابد – اما پس از محاسبه قیمت‌های بالاتر، افزایش واقعی خرید خریداران تنها 1.1 درصد پیش‌بینی می‌شود. این موضوع اهمیت بیشتری برای خریداران می‌دهد که بدانند برای چه چیزی پول می‌پردازند و آیا فروش واقعاً یک معامله است. دینش گاوری، یک مارک، "هنوز زمان خوبی برای خرید است. فقط باید کمی مراقب باشید."
items.summary_original: Black Friday deals are everywhere, but a sale price does not always mean real savings. With budgets under pressure, amid a persisting affordability crisis and rising fuel prices with the raging Iran conflict, shoppers are looking for ways to stretch their money during the holiday shopping season this year. The forecasts point to a season of cautious spending. Visa Business and Economics Insights expects holiday sales to increase 4.5% from last year — but after accounting for higher prices, the actual increase in what shoppers buy is projected to be just 1.1%. That makes it all the more important for shoppers to know what they’re paying for and whether a sale is truly a deal. "It's still a good time to shop. He advised shoppers to set a budget and research prices before making a purchase, especially for big-ticket items. items.summary: استروب تالبوت، معاون سابق وزیر امور خارجه که تخصص عمیق او در مورد اتحاد جماهیر شوروی، سیاست خارجی ایالات متحده را قبل از اینکه رهبری مؤسسه بروکینگز را بر عهده بگیرد، شکل داد، پنجشنبه در سن 80 سالگی درگذشت. پسر تالبوت، دوین تالبوت، گفت که پدرش پس از یک بیماری طولانی در خانه اش در ایست همپتون، نیویورک، به نقل از آسوشیتد پرس، در آرامش درگذشت. تالبوت که اهل اوهایو است، حرفه روزنامه نگاری خود را به عنوان کارآموز در مجله تایم در حالی که در دانشگاه ییل و آکسفورد تحصیل می کرد، آغاز کرد، جایی که با رئیس جمهور آینده بیل کلینتون هم اتاقی بود. کلینتون بعداً به شوخی گفت که کار او در آپارتمان مشترک آنها این بود که هر روز صبح صبحانه تالبوت درست کند. ناتو هشدار می دهد که پوتین می تواند قبل از پاسخ ارتش اروپایی حمله کند، ما را به عنوان الگوی نظامی نشان می دهد در حالی که در آن زمان، تالبوت برای ترجمه خاطرات فاش شده N.
items.summary_original: Strobe Talbott, a former deputy secretary of state whose deep expertise on the Soviet Union shaped U.S. foreign policy before he went on to lead the Brookings Institution, died Thursday at the age of 80. Talbott’s son, Devin Talbott, said his father died peacefully after a long illness at his home in East Hampton, New York, The Associated Press reported. An Ohio native, Talbott began his journalism career as an intern at Time magazine while studying at Yale and Oxford, where he was roommates with future President Bill Clinton . Clinton later joked that his job in their shared apartment was to make Talbott breakfast every morning. NATO WARNS PUTIN COULD STRIKE BEFORE EUROPEAN ARMY RESPONDS, POINTS TO US AS MILITARY MODEL While at Time, Talbott was tapped to translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev, the former Soviet leader ousted in 1964, which earned him a full-time role at the magazine. Over a 21-year career there, he focused on U.S.-Soviet relations, led the Washington bureau, and wrote as a foreign affairs columnist. In 1994, Talbott joined the Clinton administration as deputy secretary of state, helping guide U.S. relations with Russia and other post-Soviet states. In a statement, Bill Clinton said no one was better suited to advise him on Russian affairs than Talbott, noting that former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton also relied on his counsel. The blackout came after Ukrainian strikes had damaged the Kerch Strait Bridge last week, disrupting a key Russian military supply route, and as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Moscow was preparing another large-scale attack on Ukraine. Russian-controlled utilities blamed the Crimea blackout on an accident at energy facilities outside the region, after reports of explosions and air raid sirens sounded across the Black Sea peninsula, according to the Kyiv Post . items.summary_original: Under a cloak of secrecy, two American presidents made surprise Thanksgiving visits to war zones, bringing a taste of home to U.S. troops serving thousands of miles from their families. Sixteen years apart, President George W. Bush celebrated with American troops in Iraq in 2003, while President Donald Trump served Thanksgiving dinner to service members in Afghanistan in 2019. Both visits were carried out under tight secrecy, catching troops by surprise as they spent the holiday far from home. Trump secretly traveled to Bagram Airfield in Afghanistan on Nov. 28, 2019, when he served turkey, posed for photos and thanked American troops for their sacrifices amid the ongoing war. INSIDE TRUMP’S INTIMATE MEETING WITH NATION’S BRAVEST SOLDIERS DURING WHIRLWIND TEXAS TRIP "There's nowhere I'd rather celebrate this Thanksgiving than right here with the toughest, strongest, best and bravest warriors on the face of the Earth," Trump told the troops at the time, later adding, "And you don't even know how much the people of our country love and respect you." The visit came as roughly 12,000 American troops remained in Afghanistan more than 18 years after the U.S. invasion. And members of Congress who spoke with Fox News Digital about that special day are no different. "You know, elections can be a bumpy road in many ways, and it's easy to take a shot at somebody who's running — we put ourselves out there. items.summary_original: A former adviser to Iran's nuclear negotiating team accused Ukraine on Thursday of orchestrating a deadly drone attack in Kuwait to prove its worth to President Donald Trump, as Tehran continued to deny responsibility. And while Kuwaiti and Italian officials blamed Iran for the strike, which killed two Italian defense technicians and wounded two others, Iran’s embassy in Rome warned against "false flag" operations it said were aimed at widening the Persian Gulf conflict and now drawing Europe into the crisis. Mohammad Marandi, who served as an adviser during talks with the U.S. in Pakistan and has been dubbed Iran's " English-language mouthpiece ," claimed Ukrainian forces were operating across the Middle East, including in northern Iraq and Syria, also in remarks reported by the Fars News Agency, which is affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). items.summary_original: Thanksgiving is a day of celebration and spending time with family for the vast majority of Americans, but for several students on college campuses across the country, the national holiday is a source of anguish that is being expressed in the form of protests and counter-programming events. On Nov. 18, George Washington University hosted an event called "Breaking Bread: The Cost of Celebration" that was described as a chance for students to examine Thanksgiving, Christmas and Independence Day through an intersectional lens, including experiences of "belonging, exclusion, cultural erasure, and historical harm." "Through facilitated dialogue and shared reflection, students will engage in meaningful conversations about historical memory, social responsibility, and the complexities of celebrating within a diverse society," the student life event description read. At the University of Wisconsin at Milwaukee, the American Indian Student Center Electa Quinney Institute for American Indian Education hosted a Nov. 17 event called "AlterNative Giving," which was described as "a community gathering that offers a meaningful alternative to the traditional Thanksgiving narrative. Instead of focusing on colonial histories, we come together to honor Indigenous ways of knowing, being, and giving." Britain's Ministry of Defence has written to former service members to verify their contact information and military skills to ensure the country is prepared for a national emergency or potential conflict, Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting confirmed Friday. The outreach comes as the International Institute for Strategic Studies warned Thursday that suspected Russian-directed sabotage across Europe could trigger a "mass-casualty event." Researchers warned that a major attack could spark calls for retaliation and divide European governments. "I want the country to be alert, not alarmed," Streeting told BBC Radio 4's "Today" program. "You can't not look at what's going on in Europe and not be concerned about a threat environment which has deteriorated in recent years and is sadly increasing," he said. items.summary_original: North Korea has temporarily halted shipments of ballistic missiles and artillery shells to Russia following diplomatic friction between the two allies over Moscow's outreach to South Korea, Ukrainian military intelligence said Thursday. According to Ukraine's GUR military intelligence agency, North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui announced the freeze on KN-23 ballistic missile and artillery deliveries last month after Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko suggested Moscow would help de-escalate tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang, Reuters reported. Choe demanded that Russia clarify its policy toward South Korea, GUR said, though Reuters noted it could not independently verify the report or confirm public remarks from either official. PUTIN'S WAR DEATH TOLL REPORTEDLY TOPS 700,000 AS RUSSIA SCRAMBLES FOR RECRUITS The reported pause also suspends Russian military flights over North Korea and stalls a Kremlin request to expand North Korea's troop deployment in Russia from roughly 8,500 to 50,000, according to the outlet. Rudenko, who oversees Asian relations, said last month that Seoul had signaled interest in normalizing ties and resuming direct flights with Moscow once the Ukraine war ends. Despite the reported freeze, North Korean troops remain active in Russia, with 11th Corps units serving in the Kursk region and a missile unit operating in Voronezh since mid-summer, GUR said. items.summary_original: As Americans across the country sit down to Thanksgiving dinner just weeks after Democrats' midterm sweep drastically reshaped the political landscape going into 2027, conversations about politics and the economy could turn tense. Dr. Joel Davis Brown, a leadership expert, executive coach and author who studies how people communicate and navigate conflict, says swapping out the word "but" when discussing controversial topics can help keep the discussions civil. "‘But’ shows disagreement," Brown told Fox News Digital. "It’s a way of telling the person that what they said should not be heard, and it really stifles conversation." Instead, Brown suggests trying "yes, and." That doesn’t mean you have to agree, he said. Rather, it signals that you’ve heard the other person and leaves room to share a different view. "‘Yes, I’ve heard you and I have a different opinion,’" Brown said. "We can listen to varying opinions." FOOD PRICES ARE RISING BEFORE THANKSGIVING. AN ECONOMIST SHARES WAYS TO SAVE If a hot-button topic comes up, Brown recommends asking the person to "tell me more about that." The question, he says, can help you understand how someone arrived at their view instead of turning the exchange into a debate. He also cautions against opening with "I disagree," which can put people "in an oppositional place" before they have fully heard one another. A source familiar with the matter told The Times of Israel that the airline is being allowed back into Israeli airspace "under new security arrangements." The development comes after Transportation Minister Miri Regev decided this week that FlyDubai flights to Israel can resume pending clearance from Shin Bet, Mossad and Israel's National Security Council, the outlet reported. A FlyDubai spokesperson told Reuters that the flights will begin again on Dec. 3. FlyDubai flights to Israel have been suspended since FlyDubai Flight FZ1073 on Sept. 30, when a co-pilot allegedly attacked his captain. "Since the incident occurred, the company has continuously monitored air quality in real time using automatic ambient air quality monitoring (AQM) stations, which the company has installed in the Phra Khanong, Bang Na, and Bang Nam Phueng areas to measure air quality around the refinery resulting from operations," the company wrote. items.summary_original: Egyptian authorities said Thursday that a driver suspected of causing a fuel tanker crash in Cairo — sparking a massive inferno described by a witness as "God’s hellfire" and leaving 31 dead — has been taken into custody. The deadly blaze erupted Wednesday during rush hour on a major highway surrounding the Egyptian capital, burning 27 vehicles and also leaving 26 injured. As of Thursday, traffic on the Ring Road returned to normal after most of the wreckage was cleared. "It was God’s hellfire on the Ring Road," Salah Ahmed, a microbus driver who witnessed the inferno, told The Associated Press. "People are still in shock." Another witness said to Reuters that victims were found trapped in their vehicles as "they did not have time to get out." STATE DEPARTMENT PRESSES EGYPT TO RESPECT RELIGIOUS FREEDOM AS CHRISTIAN CONVERT FACES POSSIBLE EXECUTION Video footage taken near the scene showed a blaze completely engulfing the highway as people gathered to look at the flames. Egyptian prosecutors said in a statement that authorities had detained the driver of a vehicle suspected of causing the fuel tanker to overturn, which resulted in the fire. They said the driver told investigators he was speeding between lanes when he hit the oil tanker in the rear right. Surging prices of ham and eggnog, in particular, could put a damper on some holiday favorites. "Most of the biggest increases are things like fruits, vegetables and meats," Volpe said. Researchers identified at least 490,000 registered military deaths by late September 2026. items.summary_original: Attacks targeting Christians across Europe rose 44% last year, according to a new report from the Vienna-based Observatory on Intolerance and Discrimination Against Christians in Europe (OIDAC). Their research documented 2,465 anti-Christian hate crimes and incidents in 2025, with France , England and Wales, Germany and Austria recording the highest totals. "Our primary concern with the new data is that anti-Christian attacks that target persons, individuals themselves, have risen," OIDAC executive director Anja Tang told Fox News Digital. "Clergy and people responsible for places of worship were those who were most attacked and also where numbers increased most strongly." CHRISTIAN WOMAN PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO NEW 'ORWELLIAN' CHARGES FOR STANDING AND SILENT PRAYER She added, "These would be people who were present, were visible, recognizable as Christians and kind of associated with a church." Tang noted that while OIDAC’s numbers are "quite conservative," saying "aggression against individuals is highly underreported" across Europe. The group said French authorities recorded a 70% increase in attacks on individuals, the highest in Europe, although Tang notes the French government has not yet published a detailed explanation of the increase. OIDAC argues the increase in attacks against individuals warrants separate attention from incidents involving vandalism, theft and arson targeting religious property. items.summary_original: A leading evangelical Christian leader has embarked on a journey to trace the descendants of Jews forcibly converted to Catholicism in Spain and Portugal during the Inquisition around 500 years ago, hoping to help those of Hispanic and Latino descent, known as Anussim or crypto-Jews, rediscover their Jewish roots. Through her film, "The Lost Jews of the Inquisition," Laurie Cardoza-Moore told Fox News Digital that she hopes to help people like herself uncover a history they may not even know their families carry. She says the Israeli government believes there could be millions of "Anussim," or hidden Jews. "Some know their family history, while others don’t," she said. CHRISTIAN LEADERS HOLD EMERGENCY SUMMIT IN JERUSALEM TO CONFRONT GLOBAL RISE IN ANTISEMITISM Emmy Award-winning documentary filmmaker and host of the television show "Focus on Israel," Cardoza-Moore also serves as president of Proclaiming Justice to the Nations (PJTN). She is also a member of the Tennessee Textbook and Instructional Materials Quality Commission. For Cardoza-Moore, the journey began in 2002, in the aftermath of 9/11, when she decided to introduce a resolution in the Tennessee state legislature expressing support for Israel in its war on terror. The following year, she was invited by the Jewish Federation of Nashville on a mission to Israel. items.summary_original: The Trump administration has renewed internal discussions about potentially targeting senior Iranian regime leaders in strikes that some officials believe could end the ongoing war, according to reports. Citing a U. S. official and another source, NBC News reported Tuesday that some officials believe eliminating senior figures could pressure Tehran to end the conflict by showing that Washington can locate and strike the regime's leadership at any time. items.summary_original: Excerpts from the late Pope Francis ' private diary published Tuesday reveal that the pontiff endured a two-year spiritual crisis beginning in 2021, writing that he felt tempted by the devil and struggled with the weight of wielding power over the Catholic Church. The 160-page volume, "The Private Diary of Pope Francis," was compiled by Cardinal Victor Fernandez and spans entries from December 1992 through August 2024 — eight months before Francis died in April 2025 at age 88 — marking the first papal diary made public since the 1960s. In a December 2022 entry, Francis described his crisis as "all mixed with governance issues, pressure regarding decisions to make, and aridity and desolation," adding that he resisted becoming a leader "who uses others like puppets." "Last night I saw the entrance to Hell," he wrote in the 2018 entry. "I peeked in to look a little, and it terrified me. I grabbed the Rosary as a weapon. I thank the Lord for this help." items.summary_original: As antisemitism surges across the United States and around the world in the wake of Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023, massacre, policy strategist and public speaker Gabe Groisman is urging American Jews to stand their ground and fight for the future of their community — and the soul of the nation. In his new book, "The Jewish Fight for America," Groisman, a former mayor of Bal Harbour, Florida, explores the history of American Jews and their contributions to the country, arguing that despite rising antisemitism, they should confront the tide of hate and stand firm in their rightful place. "The first fight we have to take on here in the U.S. is to strengthen the community, to try to teach our brothers and sisters about who we are as a people," Groisman told Fox News Digital. "Then we can get to the part of why the Land of Israel is important to us, why Jewish sovereignty over the Land of Israel, which is the State of Israel today, is an integral part of who we are as Jews in America or anywhere in the world." CHRISTIAN ZIONISTS TAKE ON ANTI-ISRAEL ‘PROPAGANDA’ FROM BIBLICAL HEARTLAND One of the book’s chapters opens with quotes from Genesis. Groisman explained that powerful forces are seeking to distance American Jews from Israel. On the left, he said, a movement is seeking to "unlearn Zionism," while on the right, critics attack Zionism through the lens of dual loyalty.
